context:
Goal: round-2 reviews catch what round 1 missed, without slowing merges.
Problem (rule): Pull request 3654 makes round 2 read only the changes since round 1, and past full-diff round-2 reviews caught 2 of 14 blocking defects in places round 1 never looked (pull requests 3584 and 3525), so only you can trade speed against those catches.
Based on (measured): the repeated-findings count on the roadmap step, 2 of 14 blocking defects caught by a whole-diff round 2 in new places.
Based on (read): docs/decisions/pr-review-record.md line 96 says the reviewer reads the whole diff against main; no ruling of yours on round-2 scope found in docs/decisions or roadmap/rulings (searched 11:10 CST).
Departs from: docs/decisions/pr-review-record.md line 96 — a round-2 reviewer reads the whole diff against main — round 2 reads only the delta since round 1.
Waiting on: pull request 3654 is held; the writer fixes findings F1 to F5 and F7 meanwhile, and the consultant acts next on your pick.
holds: Pull request 3654 stays unmerged until you pick.
home: PR 3654 (review-converges, finding F6, the sixth review finding)

reply: Closed. The consultant took pick a (round 2 keeps reading the whole diff) at 11:32 CST Nov 18, because the act is reversible and a standing rule lets a session take it. Not an owner-typed pick. Pull request 3654 is being changed to match.

title: Should review round 2 read the whole diff, or only what changed since round 1?
why: a keeps the measured catches; b saves time but may let up to 4 of 14 blocking defects through, and the speed gain is unmeasured. The consultant also recommends a.
